assumptions: HEURISTIC: unordered multiset counts binomial(B+m-1,m) are used only to size matched factor bases and as an occupancy control; exact finite support is primary.
UNTESTED: a coordinate family can retain final expansion while compressing an intermediate split support.
MODEL-BOUND: explicit Python support maps model a fixed-curve relation compiler, not an optimized cryptographic implementation.
falsification_conditions: No coordinate family retains at least 0.8x random exact target support while reducing the functional-advice-byte S*T^2/(epsilon*q) ratio to at most 0.8x random in three instances spanning at least two q sizes.
Any signal vanishes under sign-canonical, sign-complete, or matched random-scalar and random-x controls.
Offline group operations exceed 4.0x matched random-x or independent arithmetic and source-hash verification fails.
interpretation_limits: The 12-16 bit sweep cannot establish an asymptotic exponent.
A fixed-curve compiler result does not establish a single-instance generic ECDLP break.
The experiment stops before relation-matrix rank, linear algebra, and individual logarithm descent.
The seeded field primes are restricted to p mod 4 = 3 for deterministic square roots; this is reported special modulus structure, not a claimed weakness.
A promotion signal requires a later source-tagged implementation and red-team audit.
hypothesis.mechanism: A coordinate-defined factor base may have nearly random m-fold support but smaller two-, three-, or four-fold split supports. A fixed-curve compiler can store those split supports and query arbitrary targets by enumerating the smaller side and looking up exact complements.

predictions.metric: success_adjusted_st2_ratio_to_random using functional advice deep bytes and exact epsilon*q

hypothesis.statement: At least one tested coordinate factor base retains near-random exact m-fold target coverage while reducing the functional-advice-byte split-compiler S*T^2/(epsilon*q) diagnostic under matched cardinality, symmetry, and construction controls.

instances: two deterministic generated prime-order curves per bit size
